newsitem.title: USA: Kasparov and Deep Blue to start re-match.
newsitem.headline: Kasparov and Deep Blue to start re-match.

text.p: World chess champion Garry Kasparov and the strongest chess-playing computer revive their rivalry Saturday when they play the first game of their $1.1 million six-game rematch in New York.

In their contest in Philadelphia in February 1996, the IBM supercomputer Deep Blue won the first game, but the Russian grandmaster recovered with three wins and two draws in the remaining games to win the match.

Kasparov, considered by most experts to be the best player in the history of chess, has no advance information of Deep Blue's most recent games or the improvements made to its program. Deep Blue, an IBM RS/6000 SP parallel processor with specialized microchips for chess, calculates twice as fast as it did last year, at rate of hundreds of millions of moves per second.
IBM computer scientists have also infused Deep Blue with more knowledge of chess with the help of full-time grandmaster consultant Joel Benjamin, a former U.S. champion.

The human player won the right to play with the white pieces in Saturday's game starting at 3 p.m. EDT (1900 GMT) and will have the advantage of the first move, similar to holding serve in tennis. Each game can last as long as six hours.
The winner of the 6-game match will collect $700,000 and the loser $400,000. The match ends on May 11.
